facts.text: On this date in 1522, the Victoria limped into Seville with 18 survivors — the first ship to circumnavigate the globe. It left with 270 men.
On this date in 1995, Cal Ripken Jr. broke Lou Gehrig's consecutive games record. Baltimore's population that year: 702,000. Today it sits below 570,000.
Tokyo's greater metropolitan area holds 37 million people — more than the entire population of Canada — yet its murder rate is lower than that of Zurich.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Jakarta than in all of Australia. Indonesia is now building a new capital, Nusantara, specifically because Jakarta is sinking into the Java Sea.
The country with the world's highest median age is not Japan. It is Monaco, where the median resident is over 55 — a city-state with no maternity ward of its own.
On this day in 1869, the Philadelphia Savings Fund Society became the first US savings bank to install a dedicated stock ticker — Wall Street's pulse, beating inside a savings institution.
On September 6, 1995, the Dow Jones closed above 4,700 for the first time. It would cross 10,000 less than four years later.

The entire US Treasury bond market — roughly $27 trillion — reprices every time a single auction clears. One number, set by competitive bids, moves the cost of borrowing for everything from mortgages to municipal debt.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway once held more US Treasury bills than the Federal Reserve itself, a quiet inversion of who actually backstops American short-term debt.
The Dutch East India Company's 1602 IPO raised 6.4 million guilders. Adjusted for economic weight, it remains the largest capital raise in history — dwarfing any modern tech listing.

On this date in 1869, John Wesley Hyatt patented celluloid — the first synthetic plastic, born from a quest to replace ivory in billiard balls. Every plastic object you touch traces its lineage to that one game.

On this date in 1522, the Victoria limped into Seville with 18 survivors, completing the first circumnavigation of Earth. The ship's log was off by one full day — time zones wouldn't explain why for another three centuries.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your bones are not static scaffolding. The entire adult skeleton replaces itself approximately every decade, driven by cells that continuously dissolve old bone and deposit new.
Light takes eight minutes to reach Earth from the Sun, but the photons began their journey inside the Sun's core up to 100,000 years ago — trapped, scattered, and redirected before finally escaping.

On this day in 1522, Magellan's ship Victoria completed the first circumnavigation of Earth — with 18 survivors from 270. The journey took 1,082 days and proved the planet was larger than almost anyone had guessed.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates what we call 'ancient' Mesoamerican civilization by three centuries.

On this day in 1901, President McKinley was shot at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo. He lingered for eight days — long enough that his doctors' optimism made the world believe he'd survive, then didn't.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was born roughly 2,500 years after Khufu's tomb was sealed, and died 2,050 years before 1969.

The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before the lightbulb. Alexander Bain's 'electric printing telegraph' transmitted images across wires while Abraham Lincoln was still a country lawyer.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable in a single word to English, it carries grief, nostalgia, and yearning fused into one.

On this day in 1522, the remnant of Magellan's fleet completed the first circumnavigation of Earth. They returned with a vocabulary problem: they'd lost an entire calendar day, which no word then existed to describe.
Petrichor (n.): the smell of rain on dry earth. Coined in 1964 by Australian scientists Isabel Bear and Richard Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid in the veins of the gods.

On this day in 1899, the word 'aspirin' was registered as a trademark by Bayer. It derives from Spiraea, the genus of meadowsweet plant yielding salicylic acid — the 'a' prefix simply meaning without acetyl's harshness.

On this date in 2017, China's People's Bank declared ICOs illegal and ordered all completed token sales to refund investors — triggering a 20% single-day drop in Ethereum's price and briefly wiping $50B from total crypto market cap.

On this date in 2021, El Salvador became the first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender, requiring all businesses to accept it — a mandate so poorly received domestically that 80% of citizens surveyed by the Central American University opposed it.

Bitcoin's base layer has never processed more than ~7 transactions per second by design. Visa handles ~65,000 at peak. The entire global Bitcoin settlement layer moves less volume per second than a single mid-sized gas station on a Saturday.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit Ethereum's code — it exploited Solidity's reentrancy pattern in a third-party contract. Ethereum's hard fork to recover funds was approved by miners controlling ~85% of hashrate, revealing how social consensus overrides code immutability.

Satoshi Nakamoto's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — a London Times headline from January 3, 2009 — serving simultaneously as a timestamp proof and an editorial on why Bitcoin was built.

On this date in 2016, DeepMind's WaveNet paper was published — a generative audio model so computationally expensive it took 90 minutes to synthesize one second of speech. It now runs in real time on consumer hardware.
On this date in 2023, GPT-4's system card revealed the model had scored in the 90th percentile on the Uniform Bar Exam — a benchmark its predecessor GPT-3.5 had failed outright just months earlier.

The entire English Wikipedia is roughly 4GB of text. GPT-3 was trained on approximately 45TB of filtered web data — about 11,000 Wikipedias — and that figure looks modest compared to models trained afterward.
Backpropagation was described in a 1974 PhD thesis by Paul Werbos, ignored for over a decade, and only became foundational after Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams independently republished it in 1986.

AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins in 2022 — essentially the entire known protein universe. The experimental databases accumulated those structures over 50 years; the inference run took weeks.
